summary: A 60-foot International Derrick tower first built in 1933 in Wickaboxet State Forest, moved about 1950 behind the West Greenwich fire station; standing, not climbable, on the NHLR since 2005.

facts.design: 60-foot International Derrick tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab

access.note: Stands behind the West Greenwich fire station on fire department property. Not fenced, but the 2016 register visit report says it should not be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Not to be climbed, per the 2016 visit report on the register. The cab holds radio equipment and the fire station siren.

events.note: Originally constructed in the Wickaboxet State Forest. The register's summary box gives 1950 as the build year, which conflicts with its own description.
Moved to the West Greenwich Fire Station, behind which it still stands.
A battery-operated radio set was loaned to the West Greenwich Fire Company for the tower (1952-53 state report, as quoted by Forest Lookouts).
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: June 2, 2005 (US 640, RI 2).

A restoration grant was presented to the owners, the West Greenwich fire department. The report gives the grant in the same passage that says the eastern regional conference was held in Rhode Island that summer, but does not say the grant was presented at the conference. The report does not say what work it covered.
Visit report, November 20, 2016: needs paint, wood and stairs in poor shape, glass broken in some windows, should not be climbed; the cab holds radio equipment and the siren.

corrections.proposed: 1933 built in Wickaboxet State Forest; 1950 relocated to the West Greenwich Fire Station
corrections.why: The register description says the tower was originally constructed in 1933 in Wickaboxet State Forest and moved in 1950. The 1950 date is the move. The register's Built field still reads 1950, so the record should say so.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's summary box says Built 1950, but its description says the tower was originally constructed in 1933 in Wickaboxet State Forest and moved to the fire station in 1950. The FFLA Instagram post repeats 1933 and 1950. The story uses 1933 for construction and 1950 for the move.

sources.title: Former Fire Lookout Sites, Rhode Island list

notes_for_editor: The 1933 date is the register's description and is repeated in the FFLA Instagram post. A Rhode Island ruins group's post, seen only as a search snippet and not read, dates the original Wickaboxet tower to 1934. It is not cited because it was not read. Worth checking if the record is revised. The 2016 visit report is the only condition report and is 10 years old. The register's coordinates (41.61944, -71.64361) differ slightly from the FFLOS list (41.61488, -71.63439). The register's 'Built' field of 1950 conflicts with its description, so the brief's 1950 build date is wrong. The 'not staffed since before 1950' wording is the register's own. The NHLR detail page for Nooseneck is a 2016-era visit report. Its Facebook 'siren is making its triumphant comeback' post was seen only in search results and is not used. The FFLA 2005 report says the restoration grant went to the owners; the work it paid for is not named anywhere in the sources read. NHLR detail page at www.nhlr.org Lookout.aspx?id=672 returned HTTP 500 and was not read.
